subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support this opt-in maintenance-specific config plus the generic command-queue onTaskTimeout hook, or should deferred maintenance use a narrower existing host timeout and abort contract?
rationale: The patch is coherent and proven, but repository policy sets a high bar for new config and shared API surfaces, while enabling a default timeout could break plugins with legitimately long maintenance runs.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Land the current disabled-by-default setting and synchronous queue hook, accepting that affected users must configure the bound explicitly.

options.title: Reuse host timeout policy
options.body: Replace the new config and generic callback with an owner-selected existing timeout and abort primitive, with explicit fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Define cancellation first
options.body: Pause the PR until the context-engine cancellation and late-side-effect contract is standardized across maintenance and compaction.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Land the current disabled-by-default setting and synchronous queue hook, accepting that affected users must configure the bound explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the documented context-engine owner and merged the background-maintenance lifecycle that this PR extends.
